_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 13. Continues Saadia's signature moves: הנגבה = 'the qibla / the south', אלקבלה. v.18 חברא = 'Hebron' (geographic identifier).

translations.1: And Abram went up from Egypt — he and his wife and all that he had, and Lot with him — toward the qibla (the south).
translations.2: And Abram was very weighty with cattle, with silver, and with gold.
translations.3: And he went on his journeys, from the qibla (the south), as far as Beth-El, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Beth-El and the Ai;
translations.4: to the place of the altar which he had made there at first; and Abram called there upon the name of God.
translations.5: And Lot also, who was going with Abram, had sheep and cattle and tents.
translations.6: And the land was not able to bear them both to dwell together; for their possessions were many, and they could not dwell together.
translations.7: And there was a quarrel between the herdsmen of Abram's cattle and the herdsmen of Lot's cattle; and the Canaanites and the Perizzites were at that time dwelling in the land.
translations.8: Until Abram said to Lot: 'Let there be no quarrel between me and you, nor between my herdsmen and your herdsmen — for we are kinfolk.
translations.9: Is not all the land before you? Separate from me; if [you go] left, I will go right; and if [you go] right, I will go left.'
translations.10: And Lot lifted up his eyes, and saw all the plain of the Jordan — that it was all watered — before God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah — like the garden of God, like the land of Egypt, as you come to Zoar.
translations.11: And Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Jordan; and he journeyed from the east; and each one separated from his brother.
translations.12: Abram dwelt in the land of Canaan; and Lot dwelt in the towns of the plain, and pitched his tent as far as Sodom.
translations.13: And the men of Sodom were wicked and great sinners against God.
translations.14: Then God said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him: 'Lift up your eyes, and look from the place where you are — northward, and southward, and eastward, and westward;
translations.15: for all the land which you see, to you I shall give it, and to your offspring forever.
translations.16: And I shall make your offspring as the dust of the earth; so that, if a man should be able to count the dust of the earth, then your offspring also shall be counted.
translations.17: Arise, walk through the land — its length and its breadth — for to you I shall give it.'
translations.18: And Abram pitched his tent, and came and settled in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron; and he built there an altar to God.
